name: Kandisort 2.4 instructions for use
menuSub: EU AI Act, Regulation 2024/1689 · 6 files · 3 pages
description: Instructions for use, with guidance for deployers, for Kandisort 2.4, a high-risk AI system that screens and ranks job applications (EU AI Act, Annex III, point 4(a), employment). Kandisort reads text CVs only and uses no biometric data.
notice: Example files loaded. The two AI Act excerpts are real Official Journal text; the Kandisort model card, risk register, logging specification and oversight note are fictional.

demo.find: In validation, Kandisort was 99% accurate for all applicants, regardless of age, gender or language.
demo.text: The accuracy metric is top-quartile agreement: the share of the applications that the panel placed in the top quarter that Kandisort also placed in its top quarter. Overall top-quartile agreement was 87.4%. Accuracy is lower for applicants aged 50 and over (81.7%), applicants with a career gap of more than 24 months (79.3%), applicants with education from outside the Nordic countries (80.2%) and applications in English (84.6%).
demo.say: Replace the 99% claim with the real figures from the validation report.
demo.expect: The accuracy rules (Article 15(3), Article 13) go from red to green.

demo.find:
Robustness and cybersecurity
Kandisort gives the same score when an application is uploaded again, and small changes in spelling or formatting change the score by less than 2 points. Hidden text, such as white keywords added to a CV, is detected and removed before scoring. Kandisort runs in an isolated EU cloud environment and is tested by an external security firm every year. Recruiter feedback is reviewed before it is used to train a new model version, so that manipulated feedback cannot change the model.
demo.say: Delete the whole robustness and cybersecurity paragraph.
demo.expect: The cybersecurity rules (Article 15(5)) leave the list: the page no longer covers them, so they go neutral, not red.

demo.text:
Informing workers and applicants
Before an employer starts using Kandisort, it must inform the workers' representatives and the affected workers. Deployers must also tell every applicant, in the job advertisement and in the confirmation of receipt, that Kandisort is used to rank applications. An applicant who is rejected can ask the deployer for an explanation of the role Kandisort played in the decision and the main reasons for the decision; the explanation panel and the ranking logs give the deployer what it needs to answer. Tallvik provides template notices for applicants and for workers' representatives in the deployer pack.
demo.say: Paste a new paragraph on informing workers and applicants.
demo.expect: New rules appear: informing workers' representatives and applicants (Article 26(7) and 26(11)) and the right to an explanation (Article 86).
